title: Defence Amendment (Fair Pay for Members of the ADF) Bill 2017
short_title: Defence Amendment (Fair Pay for Members of the ADF) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change the Defence Act 1903 to protect Australian Defence Force members' pay by tying it to the larger of annual parliamentary pay rises or the Consumer Price Index.
Currently, the Defence Minister sets ADF pay under section 58B of the Defence Act 1903, with no right of appeal, and ADF members cannot collectively bargain like other Australian workers.
The bill responds to a recent ministerial decision that left ADF wages below the cost of living for three years, which the sponsor calls an effective pay cut.
changes: Links ADF pay increases to the higher of parliamentary allowance increases or CPI.
Removes the Minister's arbitrary pay assessment by setting a formula for annual wage increases.
Ensures ADF pay does not fall below the cost of living.
summary.affected: Members of the Australian Defence Force.
